description:
## Task: TRD-023
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-0eac69b3-foreman-mcp-work-ingress-and-global-run-slot-queue.md#trd-023
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-0eac69b3-foreman-mcp-work-ingress-and-global-run-slot-queue.md#req-001

--- TRD Context ---
### 2.1 Alternatives Considered

#### Option A — Simplest: MCP as a thin HTTP client over the existing Task path (REJECTED)

The MCP server calls `task.create` then `task.approve` on behalf of the caller, mapping `prompt` onto the task's `description` field.

- **Pros:** No new aggregate, no new command types, no changes to `RunAdmission` or `RunExecutor`. Two days of work.
- **Cons:** Fails REQ-006 through REQ-008 outright. `description` is not rendered into any bundled prompt template, and the assigns map in `prompt_template_assigns/4` has no key that would surface it, so the prompt would be accepted and silently discarded — the worst possible failure mode. It also inherits the full approval/dispatch ceremony the PRD is trying to escape, and every submission mints a Beads-shaped task the `BeadsOrphanJanitor` will later reason about.
- **Risk:** HIGH. Ships a feature that appears to work and does not.

#### Option B — Most thorough: replace Task with a unified WorkItem model (REJECTED)

Delete `Aggregates.Task`, introduce `WorkItem` as the single pre-run identity, re-key `Identity.run_id/2` off `(project_id, external_id, nonce)`, and migrate the Beads integration onto it.

- **Pros:** One ingress, one model, no divergence risk. The end state the PRD's §2.4 dead-code findings point toward.
- **Cons:** `run_id` derivation changes, which invalidates the deterministic-retry contract that `CommandGateway.enrich_task_retry_with_bound_run/2` and `BootReconciliation.scan_task_run_orphans/0` both depend on. `BeadsWatcher` dedupe (`ProjectionStore.get_task(external_id:)`) and `BeadsOrphanJanitor`'s terminal-task check would both need reconstruction against the new anchor. 78 lib files and 85 test files mention task. This is a quarter of work before the first MCP call succeeds.
- **Risk:** HIGH. The valuable part of the PRD is reachable without it.

#### Option C — Parallel lean ingress converging at admission (CHOSEN)

A new `WorkRequest` aggregate is the pre-run identity for agentic submissions. It emits one event carrying everything a run needs, and hands `RunAdmission.start/2` the same payload shape the Task path already hands it. Both paths converge at admission; nothing below admission knows which ingress it came from except one `source` field consumed by `RunExecutor`'s lifecycle hooks.

- **Pros:** `RunAdmission`, `CommandRouter`, `Aggregates.Run`, `Aggregates.Project`, `RunSupervisor`, `PrGate`, `PrAssociate`, and `StuckDetector` require **zero** changes — verified: `pr_gate.ex`, `pr_associate.ex`, `aggregates/pr_association.ex`, and `stuck_detector.ex` contain no reference to task at all, and `Project.active_run_reservations` is keyed by `run_id`. `RunExecutor` needs one branch. The Beads path is untouched, so its dedupe and orphan-janitor anchors keep working. Each PR is independently shippable.
- **Cons:** Two ingress paths to maintain, and `Aggregates.Run` keeps a field named `task_id` that now holds either a task id or a work id. The field is not renamed because doing so would rewrite the event schema for every historical run.
- **Risk:** LOW. The convergence point is a single function with an existing, tested contract.

### 2.2 Chosen Architecture (Option C)

#### 2.2.1 Component Boundaries

**New library modules (under `packages/foreman_server/lib/foreman_server/`):**

| Path | Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `aggregates/run_slots.ex` | `ForemanServer.Aggregates.RunSlots` | Event-sourced global admission gate on stream `run_slots:global`. State is `RunSlots.State` (`defstruct [:capacity, holders: %{}, waiters: []]`). Commands `run_slots.acquire`, `run_slots.release`, `run_slots.remove_waiter`. Structurally modeled on `Aggregates.BeadsDbLease`: acquire-or-enqueue is one atomic command so lost wakeups are impossible, and release-with-waiters emits a **single** `RunSlotTransferred` event rather than a release followed by a promote. |
| `aggregates/work_request.ex` | `ForemanServer.Aggregates.WorkRequest` | Pre-run identity for agentic submissions on stream `work:<work_id>`. State is `WorkRequest.State` (`defstruct [:work_id, :status, :project_id, :run_id, :bound_run_id, :submission_id, :workflow_snapshot]`). Commands `work.submit`, `work.cancel`, `work.execution_complete`, `work.execution_fail`. Statuses `submitted → queued → running → succeeded \| failed \| cancelled`. Deliberately small: four commands, no dependency graph, no annotations, no approval step — the ceremony the PRD's §2.4 identified as dead in `Aggregates.Task` is not reproduced here. |
| `work/submission.ex` | `ForemanServer.Work.Submission` | Pure function, the `WorkRequest` analogue of `Workflow.Approval.prepare/2`. Given `%{work_id, project_id, workflow, prompt}`, derives `submission_id`, computes `run_id = Identity.run_id(work_id, submission_id)`, loads the manifest via `Catalog.load(workflow <> ".yaml")`, stamps `index`/`phase_id` on each phase, and builds `workflow_snapshot` including the `input` block. Returns `{:ok, map()}` or `{:error, {:workflow_load_failed, name, reason}}`. |
| `work/run_payload.ex` | `ForemanServer.Work.RunPayload` | Single source of truth for the admission payload shape. Exposes `from_task_projection/1` and `from_work_projection/1`, both returning the same 7-key map (`run_id`, `task_id`, `project_id`, `approval_id`, `workflow_snapshot`, `phase_specs`, `source`). `Workflow.Dispatcher` is refactored to build the Task payload through `from_task_projection/1` so the two ingresses cannot drift. |
| `mcp.ex` | `ForemanServer.MCP` | Façade. Tool registry, capability advertisement, and the single `call_tool/3` entrypoint both transports share. |
| `mcp/policy.ex` | `ForemanServer.MCP.Policy` | Default-deny gate. Validates every tool name against the enabled set, refuses any dispatch whose command type is outside `CommandGateway.@allowed_operator_types`, and gates workflow writes behind `allow_workflow_writes`. `dispatch_system/2` is not reachable from any MCP code path — enforced by an architecture test. |
| `mcp/auth.ex` | `ForemanServer.MCP.Auth` | Shared bearer verifier used by the HTTP plug and the stdio entrypoint. Fails closed when `:api_bearer_token` is unset, unlike `Plugs.BearerAuth`, whose permissive behaviour is preserved for `/api`. |
| `mcp/tools.ex` | `ForemanServer.MCP.Tools` | Tool definitions: name, description, JSON Schema, handler. One module, one function per tool, no metaprogramming. |
| `mcp/stdio.ex` | `ForemanServer.MCP.Stdio` | stdio transport. Reads JSON-RPC 2.0 frames from stdin, writes to stdout, routes **all** diagnostics to Logger's stderr backend so stdout carries protocol bytes only. |
| `workflow/manifest_writer.ex` | `ForemanServer.Workflow.ManifestWriter` | Canonical serializer. Emits **only** the constructs `Workflow.Interpreter` parses: top-level `key: value` scalars, a `phases:` list at indent 0, phase entries at indent 2, phase properties at indent 4, single-level nested maps at indent 6. Validates the emitted bytes by round-tripping them through `Interpreter.load/1` before any filesystem move. |
| `workflow/catalog_writer.ex` | `ForemanServer.Workflow.CatalogWriter` | Filesystem discipline for catalog mutation: containment check against `Catalog.root/0`, `name:`-matches-stem check, write to a temp file inside the root, `File.rename/2` into place. Never partially writes a manifest. |

**New web modules (under `packages/foreman_server/lib/foreman_server_web/`):**

| Path | Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp_router.ex` | `ForemanServerWeb.MCPRouter` | Streamable HTTP transport mounted at `/mcp` via a dedicated `:mcp` pipeline (`:accepts json` + `ForemanServer.MCP.Auth` plug). Mounted outside the `:api` scope so it does not inherit `Plugs.BearerAuth`'s permissive-when-unset behaviour. |
| `controllers/work_controller.ex` | `ForemanServerWeb.WorkController` | `GET /api/work/:id` returning the work projection, mirroring `TaskController.show/2`. |
| `controllers/queue_controller.ex` | `ForemanServerWeb.QueueController` | `GET /api/queue` returning capacity, running runs, and ordered waiters. |

**Existing modules changed (surgical):**

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/foreman_server/run_admission.ex` | Add the global slot as the **outermost** gate, ahead of the existing Beads-DB lease. New return value `{:ok, :slot_queued}` alongside the existing `{:ok, :queued}`. On a lease `:queued` result, release the just-acquired slot before returning, per Decision 3. Extend `compensable_admission_error?/1` handling so a failed `run.start` releases the slot as well as the lease. |
| `lib/foreman_server/workflow/dispatcher.ex` | Add `handle_work_submitted/2` (mirrors `handle_task_dispatched/2`, routed through `Work.RunPayload.from_work_projection/1`). Add `handle_slot_promoted/2` (mirrors `handle_lease_promoted/2`, subscribing to `RunSlotTransferred`). Extend the terminal-run fan-out to dispatch `run_slots.release`. **Delete** the `put_in(state, [:pending, task_id], reason)` write and the `:pending` key — it is never read and is the current silent-drop bug. |
| `lib/foreman_server/workflow/run_executor.ex` | (a) Add `input` to `prompt_template_assigns/4` as flat `"input.prompt"` and `"input.prompt_argument"` keys, defaulting to `""` when the snapshot has no `input` block. (b) Branch `maybe_claim_task/1`, `maybe_complete_task/1`, and `maybe_fail_task/4` on `state.source`: for `:work_request`, skip the `TaskProvider` callbacks and dispatch `work.execution_complete` / `work.execution_fail` instead of the `task.*` equivalents. **The command-phase path is deliberately not touched** — command rendering stays at snapshot-freeze time in `CommandGateway`. |
| `lib/foreman_server/command_gateway.ex` | Add `work.submit` and `work.cancel` to `@allowed_operator_types` (bringing it to 9). Add `validate_aggregate_id/1` clauses for both. Add an `enrich_operator_command/1` clause for `work.submit` that calls `Work.Submission.prepare/1` and rejects client-supplied `submission_id`, `run_id`, and `workflow_snapshot` as reserved, mirroring `@reserved_approval_fields`. Extend `render_strict_fields/1` to fire when the snapshot has an `implementation` block **or** an `input` block (today it early-returns when `implementation` is nil), and extend `render_command/2`'s literal-token allow-list with `{{input.prompt}}` and `{{input.prompt_argument}}`. |
| `lib/foreman_server/aggregates/task.ex` | Remove `handle_command/2` clauses for `task.block`, `task.close`, `task.update`, `task.annotate`, `task.add_dependency`. **Retain** every `apply_event/2` clause and every `event_codec.ex` entry — the write path is removed, the read path is not, so historical streams stay decodable. |
| `lib/foreman_server/aggregates/project.ex` | Replace the hardcoded `@max_concurrent_runs 100` with a config lookup defaulting to 100, carried on the reserve command so replay stays deterministic. |
| `lib/foreman_server/projection_store.ex` | Add a `work` projection map folding the four `Work*` events, with `work_projection/1` and `list_work/0`. Add a `run_slots` projection folding the five `RunSlot*` events, with `queue_status/0`. Remove `list_workflow_tasks/0` (no callers). |
| `lib/foreman_server/run_lifecycle_reconciler.ex` | Subscribe to terminal run events for slot release alongside the existing project-reservation release. Extend the 30-second sweep to detect a promoted-but-not-started waiter and retry admission — the backstop for a dropped broadcast. |
| `lib/foreman_server/workflow/boot_reconciliation.ex` | Add `scan_run_slot_orphans/0` + `reconcile_run_slots_stream/0`, mirroring `scan_lease_orphans/0` + `reconcile_lease_stream/1`: load `run_slots:global`, drop holders and waiters whose run is absent or terminal, promote live waiters into freed slots. |
| `lib/foreman_server/event_codec.ex` | Register `WorkSubmitted`, `WorkCancelled`, `WorkExecutionCompleted`, `WorkExecutionFailed`, `RunSlotAcquired`, `RunSlotQueued`, `RunSlotReleased`, `RunSlotTransferred`, `RunSlotWaiterRemoved`. |
| `lib/foreman_server/command_router.ex` | Route stream prefixes `work:` → `Aggregates.WorkRequest` and `run_slots:` → `Aggregates.RunSlots`. |
| `lib/foreman_server/application.ex` | Add `ForemanServer.MCP` supervisor subtree. `RunSlots` needs no process — it is an aggregate, loaded on demand like `BeadsDbLease`. |
| `lib/foreman_server_web/router.ex` | Add `GET /api/work/:id`, `GET /api/queue` under `:api`. Add the `:mcp` pipeline and `/mcp` scope. |
| `lib/foreman_server_web/controllers/command_controller.ex` | Extend `@allowed_types` to match the gateway's 9, and add a test asserting the two lists are equal. |
| `config/config.exs` | `max_concurrent_runs: 3`, `max_concurrent_runs_per_project: 100`, `config :foreman_server, :mcp, enabled: false, mount: "/mcp", allow_workflow_writes: false, allow_insecure_local: false`. |
| `config/prod.exs` / `ForemanServer.ConfigProviders.Secrets` | Map `FOREMAN_API_TOKEN` → `:api_bearer_token`. This mapping does not exist today, which is why bearer auth is inert in every environment. |
| **Deleted** | `lib/foreman_server/commands/create_task.ex`, `lib/foreman_server/commands/close_task.ex`, `lib/foreman_server/events/task_closed.ex` — all three are defined and referenced nowhere; `TaskClosed` is not even registered in the codec. |

**Explicitly NOT changed (verified no coupling):**

| Module | Why untouched |
|---|---|
| `pr_gate.ex`, `pr_associate.ex`, `aggregates/pr_association.ex` | Keyed entirely by `run_id`; contain no reference to task. Work-sourced runs get PR association for free. |
| `stuck_detector.ex`, `overwatch/*.ex` | Operate on run and worker state only; no task references anywhere in the directory. |
| `task_providers/*` (Beads adapter, watcher, janitor) | The Beads reverse-sync path is out of scope by design. `WorkRequest` never touches a `TaskProvider`. |
| `aggregates/run.ex` | `run.start` requires `task_id`; work-sourced runs supply the `work_id` in that field. No schema change, no migration. |
| `aggregates/project_run_limit.ex` | Left inert rather than deleted, to keep this slice's diff focused. Flagged for removal in a follow-up. |

#### 2.2.2 Data Flow

**Admission with the global slot gate (both ingresses)**

```
Workflow.Dispatcher (on TaskDispatched | WorkSubmitted)
  │ payload = Work.RunPayload.from_task_projection/1 | from_work_projection/1
  ▼
RunAdmission.start(project_id, payload)
  │
  ├─ GATE 1 (outer, global) ─ CommandGateway.dispatch_system("run_slots.acquire",
  │      %{run_id, work_or_task_id, capacity: cfg(:max_concurrent_runs, 3)})
  │   ├─ holders < capacity → RunSlotAcquired  → continue
  │   ├─ run_id already a holder → idempotent no-op → continue
  │   └─ holders == capacity   → RunSlotQueued  → return {:ok, :slot_queued}   [no run started]
  │
  ├─ GATE 2 (inner, per Beads DB — unchanged) ─ lease.acquire
  │   ├─ :proceed → continue
  │   └─ :queued  → dispatch run_slots.release FIRST (Decision 3), then {:ok, :queued}
  │
  └─ CommandRouter.dispatch_run_start/2
        ├─ project.reserve_run   (existing per-project reservation, now configurable)
        └─ run.start → RunStarted → RunSupervisor.start_run(run_id, payload)
```

**Drain on termination**

```
RunCompleted | RunFailed | RunCancelled | RunFlaggedStuck | RunBlocked
  │
  ├─ Workflow.Dispatcher.handle_run_terminated/3
  │     ├─ BootReconciliation.run_terminated/2      (existing)
  │     ├─ lease.release / lease.remove_waiter      (existing)
  │     └─ run_slots.release                        (NEW)
  │           ├─ no waiters → RunSlotReleased
  │           └─ waiters    → RunSlotTransferred  {released_run_id, acquired_run_id}
  │                              │  (single atomic event: release + promote FIFO head)
  │                              ▼
  │                       Dispatcher.handle_slot_promoted/2
  │                              └─ RunAdmission.start/2 for acquired_run_id
  │                                    └─ RunSupervisor.start_run/2
  │
  └─ RunLifecycleReconciler (subscription + 30s sweep)
        ├─ project.release_run_reservation           (existing)
        ├─ run_slots.release                         (NEW — redundant with the above, idempotent)
        └─ sweep: holder promoted but no RunStarted after N sweeps → retry admission
              (backstop for a dropped broadcast — AC-012-3)
```

**Prompt from submit to agent**

```
MCP foreman_work_submit {workflow: "implement-trd", prompt: "<free text>"}
  │
  ▼
CommandGateway.dispatch_operator(%{type: "work.submit", payload})
  │ enrich → Work.Submission.prepare/1
  │            ├─ Catalog.load("implement-trd.yaml")     → resolved manifest
  │            ├─ run_id = Identity.run_id(work_id, submission_id)
  │            └─ workflow_snapshot.input = %{prompt: "<verbatim>",
  │                                           prompt_argument: Jason.encode!("<verbatim>")}
  ▼
  │            └─ render_strict_fields/1 → render_command/2
  │                 substitutes {{input.prompt_argument}} into command: phases
  │                 NOW, at freeze time — same place {{implementation.*}} is
  │                 already substituted today
  ▼
WorkSubmitted  (stream work:<work_id>)  — prompt AND rendered commands are now immutable
  ▼
RunExecutor.init/1 → state.plan_context ⊕ snapshot.input
  │
  ├─ prompt-type phase: read_phase_prompt/4 (Catalog .md body)
  │      → render_prompt_template/5 against assigns incl. "input.prompt"
  │
  └─ command-type phase: already-rendered command string from the snapshot
         → execute_agent/4                ◀── unchanged; no run-time rendering
```

Two substitution passes exist and they are deliberately different. Freeze-time rendering (`render_command/2`) is a **closed allow-list of literal tokens** applied once and made immutable. Run-time rendering (`render_prompt_template/5`) is a regex over a flat assigns map applied to prompt bodies only. Both are single-pass, so a prompt containing the literal text `{{run_id}}` is inert data and is never recursively expanded (AC-007-3).

#### 2.2.3 Integration Points

1. **`RunAdmission.start/2` is the convergence point.** Both ingresses call it with a payload built by `Work.RunPayload`, which is the only module allowed to construct that shape. An architecture test asserts no other module builds it inline.
2. **`Workflow.Dispatcher` is the only subscriber that starts executors.** Three clauses now feed it: `TaskDispatched`, `WorkSubmitted`, and promotions (`BeadsDbLeaseTransferred`, `RunSlotTransferred`).
3. **`CommandGateway` remains the sole mutation surface.** MCP tools call `dispatch_operator/2` exclusively; `MCP.Policy` refuses anything outside the allow-list before the call is made.
4. **`Workflow.Catalog`'s 2-second poll is the reload mechanism** for MCP workflow writes. `CatalogWriter` does not call `Catalog.reload/0` implicitly; the tool response reports whether the write has been observed by the catalog yet.

#### 2.2.4 Technology Choices

| Choice | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| MCP protocol implementation | `{:anubis_mcp, "~> 1.10"}`, with a hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 module as the documented fallback | `anubis_mcp` is the maintained successor to `hermes_mcp` (renamed at v0.14), provides both server construction and Plug/Phoenix integration, and is on Hex at 1.x. The earlier TRD-2026-e8d3f5f2 left this decision explicitly open; it is closed here. The fallback matters because the tool surface is small enough (~13 tools) that hand-rolling framing is a two-day job if the dependency review rejects the addition. |
| HTTP transport | Streamable HTTP under the existing Cowboy stack | `mix.lock` pins `plug_cowboy 2.9.0` / Cowboy 2.17.0. Bandit is an optional dep of Phoenix 1.8.9 but is **not** locked, so no server swap is implied. |
| Slot state storage | Event-sourced aggregate on a single stream | Matches `BeadsDbLease` exactly and is the only durable-queue pattern already proven in this codebase. A GenServer would repeat `ConcurrencyLimiter`'s mistake — in-memory waiters that a crash silently discards. |
| Capacity value | Carried on the acquire command, recorded on the event | Reading `Application.get_env` inside a decision function would make replay non-deterministic after an operator changes the config. Recording it makes history self-describing. |
| Slot stream granularity | One global stream, `run_slots:global` | Serializes all admission. At capacity 3 this is irrelevant; it is a throughput ceiling only at much higher capacities, and is documented as such rather than pre-optimized. |
| Manifest writing | Canonical serializer, not a YAML library | `Workflow.Interpreter` is a hand-rolled indentation-sensitive parser, not real YAML. It has no support for block scalars, anchors, flow sequences, or nesting beyond indent 6. A standard YAML emitter would produce valid YAML that this parser silently misreads. |
| Prompt storage | Verbatim in the frozen snapshot | Consistent with how `ImplementationContext` is frozen at approval time specifically to avoid re-resolution drift. |

#### 2.2.5 Telemetry Taxonomy

| Event | Measurements | Metadata |
|---|---|---|
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :acquired]` | `%{holders: n, capacity: n}` | `run_id`, `source` |
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :queued]` | `%{depth: n}` | `run_id`, `position` |
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :released]` | `%{holders: n}` | `run_id`, `reason` |
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :transferred]` | `%{depth: n}` | `released_run_id`, `acquired_run_id` |
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :waiter_removed]` | `%{depth: n}` | `run_id`, `reason` |
| `[:foreman_server, :run_slots, :reconciled]` | `%{holders_dropped: n, waiters_dropped: n}` | `phase` (`:boot` \| `:sweep`) |
| `[:foreman_server, :work, :submitted]` | `%{prompt_bytes: n}` | `work_id`, `run_id`, `workflow`, `project_id` — **never the prompt body** |
| `[:foreman_server, :work, :terminal]` | `%{duration_us: n}` | `work_id`, `run_id`, `status` |
| `[:foreman_server, :mcp, :tool, :call]` | `%{duration_us: n}` | `tool`, `outcome` — **never arguments, never the token** |
| `[:foreman_server, :mcp, :policy, :refused]` | `%{}` | `tool`, `reason` |

### 2.3 Design Decisions

**Decision 1 — `WorkRequest` is a new aggregate, not a reuse of `Task`.** Reusing `Task` would mean either resurrecting `task.approve`'s enrichment for a path that has nothing to approve, or adding a bypass flag to an aggregate whose whole problem is accumulated ceremony. A four-command aggregate is smaller than the conditional logic reuse would require.

**Decision 2 — `Aggregates.Run.task_id` is not renamed.** It now carries either a task id or a work id. Renaming it would rewrite the event schema for every historical `RunStarted`. The `source` field disambiguates, and it is the only field consumers need.

**Decision 3 — Slot outer, lease inner, and release the slot when lease-queued.** Three orderings were considered. Lease-first lets a run hold a Beads-DB mutex while waiting for capacity, blocking every other run on that database. Slot-first-and-hold lets lease-blocked runs occupy capacity while doing no work — with capacity 3 and three runs on one database, two slots sit idle. Slot-first-and-release-when-queued has neither property: a lease waiter holds nothing, and on `BeadsDbLeaseTransferred` the existing `re_dispatch_promoted/3` already re-enters `RunAdmission.start/2` from the top, which re-acquires a slot naturally. No new promotion machinery is needed for the interaction.

**Decision 4 — Task pruning removes the write path only.** `apply_event/2` clauses and `event_codec.ex` entries for `TaskUpdated`, `TaskAnnotated`, and `TaskDependencyAdded` are retained. Even though these events were never dispatched in production, removing decode support would make any stream containing them permanently unreplayable — an irreversible failure mode traded against zero benefit.

**Decision 5 — MCP fails closed on auth; `/api` does not change.** `Plugs.BearerAuth` passing through when `:api_bearer_token` is unset is deliberate for local development and is out of scope to change. `MCP.Auth` refuses to start without a token unless `allow_insecure_local: true` is explicit. This lets the MCP ingress be safe without a flag day for existing HTTP callers.

**Decision 6 — Prompt substitution for command phases happens at freeze time, not run time.** The obvious implementation is to render `command:` strings inside `RunExecutor` alongside prompt bodies. That is the wrong place. Command strings are *already* rendered at snapshot-freeze time by `CommandGateway.render_strict_fields/1` → `render_command/2`, and the frozen result is what the executor consumes. Adding a second, later rendering pass would mean two renderers with different semantics operating on the same string, and would break the invariant that a frozen snapshot is fully resolved. Extending the existing renderer instead means `RunExecutor`'s command path is untouched, the prompt is immutable from the moment `WorkSubmitted` is appended, and there is exactly one place where a command string acquires its final form.

Two facts about that renderer shape the tasks. It substitutes exactly two literal tokens, and `render_strict_fields/1` returns the snapshot unmodified when it finds no `implementation` block — which means `plan.yaml`, whose phases are command-type and which carries no implementation context, currently receives no command rendering at all. TRD-020 widens the token allow-list; TRD-019 fixes the trigger condition. TRD-018 pins the current frozen output first, because this renderer's output goes into the event store and a defect there ships into history rather than into a retryable execution.

title: test_helper.exs:20 File.rm_rf! of temp dir can crash at exit ('file already exists') when several mix test processes run concurrently
description: Seen once in 40 looped runs of run_steering_test.exs+live_steering_test.exs (LandLiveInput, #641) while other agents ran suites on the same host: the test run printed no result line and crashed at exit in test/test_helper.exs:20 (File.rm_rf! on the tmp dir: file already exists); a rerun passed. Likely concurrent mix test processes sharing a /tmp/fm-test-* path (see cwd: /tmp/fm-test-NNNN in CI logs). Single-job CI is probably unaffected. Make the tmp root per-OS-process unique (System.unique_integer/os pid) or harden cleanup; confirm the cause before changing.
close_reason: Fixed in #649: root cause was leftover read-only overview-library trees (0555 dirs) in fm-test-<pid> dirs plus OS pid reuse; File.rm_rf! at boot died on a stale dir. Per-VM dir is now claimed fresh and removed with a chmod-aware helper.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text: Pointer confirmed: packages/foreman_server/test/test_helper.exs:19-20 does vm_tmp = Path.join(System.tmp_dir!(), "fm-test-#{System.pid()}") then File.rm_rf!(vm_tmp) (raises on failure). The 'file already exists' exit crash is therefore more likely a stale fm-test-<ospid> directory from an earlier VM that reused the same OS pid (or files that rm_rf cannot remove), not two live VMs sharing one path as first guessed: PIDs are unique among live processes. Next step: capture the full message/stack on reproduction (loop the suite while leaving a read-only file under /tmp/fm-test-<pid>) before changing anything.

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (TempDirCrash). Confirmed by reproduction. The stale-pid hypothesis in the earlier comment is right; the "two live VMs share one path" guess is ruled out (no concurrency is needed to hit it).

THE CRASH, captured with the real `mix test` + the real helper:

    ** (File.Error) could not remove files and directories recursively from ".../fm-test-83748": file already exists
        (elixir 1.20.4) lib/file.ex:1768: File.rm_rf!/1
        test/test_helper.exs:20: (file)

exit 1, no result line (the VM dies while loading the helper, before any test runs).

WHY rm_rf! FAILS. "file already exists" is Erlang's name for ENOTEMPTY (:eexist): the rmdir of the ROOT found it non-empty. Elixir 1.20.4 File.rm_rf swallows each child's failure (lib/file.ex:1667-1675, "In case we can't delete, continue anyway") and reports only the root, so the real error never surfaces. The child error is :eacces: the Library publishes entries read-only (Library.Store.lock_down: files 0444, directories 0555) and unlink inside a 0555 directory is refused. Direct experiment: File.rm(facts.txt) -> {:error, :eacces}; File.rm_rf(root) -> {:error, :eexist, root}.

WHY A LEFTOVER EXISTS AT fm-test-<pid>. Every full suite leaves one. test/foreman_server/overview/tabs_test.exs "library lists the project's library entries" creates a Library entry under System.tmp_dir!() and cleans up with `on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf(root) end)` (non-bang, result never read); the helper's `after_suite(fn _ -> File.rm_rf(vm_tmp) end)` ignores the result too. Real test, old helper: after `mix test .../tabs_test.exs` (5 passed) TMPDIR holds fm-test-<pid>/overview-library-N/.foreman/library/facts-H/{entry.json,files/facts.txt} with non-writable directories. On this host at the time of writing there were 57 fm-test-<pid> dirs in $TMPDIR: 1 belongs to a running VM, 55 hold exactly one entry (a non-writable overview-library-N tree) and nothing else, 1 is empty (a killed VM). Oldest leftover: Oct 22 08:23. So tabs_test was the only source of an undeletable tree in those 55 suites.

WHY IT BITES LATER. A new VM whose OS pid equals a leftover's pid does File.rm_rf!(<that path>) at boot and dies. macOS recycles pids fast (measured ~450 new pids/s here, so the 1..99999 space wraps in ~4 minutes). Per-run hit rate = leftovers / ~99,999: ~0.06% with today's 56, rising by one per full suite and never self-healing (the crashing VM cannot clear it). The reported 1-in-40 is a ~2% draw at today's leftover count; UNVERIFIED whether the population was larger when it was seen (the failing pid was not captured anywhere I could read).

REPRODUCTION (before / after the fix, same harness):
- pid-pinned, real mix test: `exec` keeps System.pid() == $$, so seeding fm-test-$$ with a Library-shaped read-only tree and then exec'ing mix test crashes exactly as above (before) and runs "5 passed" (after).
- tight loop, 8 parallel x 40 = 320 minimal ExUnit VMs running the helper block lifted verbatim, with leftovers seeded for a random 24.9% of the pid space: BEFORE, 90 of 320 runs had a leftover at their pid and all 90 crashed with the message above (0 crashes without a leftover). AFTER the fix, 640 runs (320 at 24.9%, 320 at 50.1% seeding): 231 of them hit a leftover at their pid, 0 crashed, every VM removed its own dir and no leftover was touched.

FIX (PR follows): test/support/tmp.ex ForemanServer.TestSupport.Tmp. claim_vm_dir!/1 creates fm-test-<pid>-<8 hex> with an exclusive File.mkdir! and never inspects or clears an existing path, so a leftover of any origin cannot collide. release_vm_dir/1 (after_suite) uses remove_tree/1, which chmods each directory 0700 before reading it, never follows symlinks, tolerates only :enoent (entry already gone), returns every other errno with its path, and prints those to stderr instead of staying silent. tabs_test now cleans up with remove_tree and asserts :ok. packages/jido_harness/test/test_helper.exs does not have the pattern (ExUnit.start(exclude: ...) only; no TMPDIR, no pid-keyed path, no rm_rf!).

comments.author: ldangelo
comments.text:
PR #649 (ldangelo/foreman): https://github.com/ldangelo/foreman/pull/649 - fix for the root cause in the comment above. CI is green on every job: foreman_server (10m10s) "Result: 5105 passed (6 properties, 5099 tests), 8 excluded", jido_harness, foreman_cli. Local full suite (same command as CI, private DB, pool 4, under the shared lock): the same 5105 passed, exit 0, 381 s; compile --warnings-as-errors, format --check-formatted, credo --min-priority higher and doctor --raise all exit 0.

Mutation checks (revert, watch the new tests fail, restore): 5 mutations, each caught; reverting claim_vm_dir! to the old fm-test-<pid> + rm_rf! makes the regression test raise the production error "could not remove files and directories recursively from ...: file already exists".

Left alone, for the lead:
- 56 old-scheme fm-test-<pid> leftovers are still in this host's $TMPDIR (55 read-only Library trees, 1 empty; every pid dead when last checked, plus 1 live VM's dir that is not a leftover). They cannot collide with the new names, but a worktree still on the old helper whose pid matches one will still crash until it rebases. I did not delete them (not my slice, and a live VM's fresh dir could race a sweep).
- Adjacent hazard, UNVERIFIED (no failure observed, nothing changed): packages/jido_harness tests build scratch paths as System.unique_integer([:positive]) suffixes under the shared system tmp dir (for example jido-harness-journal-N with on_exit File.rm_rf!) and its helper has no per-VM TMPDIR, i.e. the cross-VM name collision #595 fixed for foreman_server. Two concurrent jido_harness runs could hand out the same name. Not the pattern this bead is about, so not touched.

title: [E12] True multi-repo projects and runs
description:
Decision D3: a project owns repositories[] (id, path, default branch, VCS/PR settings, optional task-provider binding) and ONE run can hold one worktree per repository and open one branch + one PR per touched repository. This is the largest and riskiest epic: the code base is single-path everywhere today - `ProjectRegistered.path` (events/project_registered.ex), `RunExecutor` derives `project_root` from plan_context or the project path (run_executor.ex:2141-2160, 2395-2412), one `state.run_worktree` with op id `wt-<run_id>` (:2270-2300), one base branch (`run_base_branch/1`, :1770), `foreman_env/4` with a single FOREMAN_WORKTREE_PATH (:2924), AutoPR/PhasePR + `PrAssociate` keyed `pr_association:<run_id>` (pr_associate.ex:34), a single scalar `merge_gate` on the Run aggregate (run.ex:37), PrMonitor per run, Review.Capture single diff (review/capture.ex:313), Jobsite.Spec single repo (spec.ex:64) and BeadsWatcher per project provider.

Design-first: spike S3 (owned by E0) writes docs/spikes/S3.md BEFORE any E12 story starts; every story depends on S3 and states what each S3 outcome changes. Defaults baked into the stories (what we expect S3 to choose): single-element repositories[] synthesised at READ time for legacy projects (no event rewrite); primary keeps `wt-<run>` and every existing env var; additive env `FOREMAN_REPOS`; per-repo `pr_association` keys; merge gate per PR (still operator-only, never MCP, per-PR head pin); partial completion expressed as per-repo PR state + derived `completed_with_errors` (no new run status); agent self-add of a repo only via operator allowlist + audit event; fan-out as N independent single-repo tasks.

Safety constraints: EventCodec REJECTS unknown keys on typed decode (event_codec.ex:238-256) so every new stored field must be a declared non-enforced struct field; a rollback after repositories were written is not replay-safe (documented). Single-repo behaviour must be byte-identical (golden tests per story). Cross-epic needs: E3 renders the `repositories` prompt assign, E9 follows the per-PR addressing contract, E15 coordinator uses repo_id and the fan-out/self-add tools, E16 consolidates CLI usage/agent_commands/MCP pins for the verbs and tools added here.

---
Plan key: E12  |  Plan: local://claude-projects-parity-plan.md (Claude Projects parity)
acceptance_criteria:
- repositories[] on projects with legacy single-path projects unchanged (read-time synthesis, replay-compat test)
- foreman project repo add|remove|list, HTTP and MCP read surfaces
- one run: N worktrees, N branches, N PRs for touched repos; per-repo association and per-PR operator-only merge gate
- env/prompt list every repo; review archive and jobsite handle several repos

title: [E12-S1] Project repositories[] model, events, projection and legacy migration
description:
A project today owns exactly one `path`: `Events.ProjectRegistered` (events/project_registered.ex) is `@enforce_keys [:project_id, :path, :task_provider]`, `Aggregates.Project` state carries `path/default_branch/task_provider/config`, and `ProjectionStore.project_projection/2` projects `project_id, path, status, archived?, default_branch, config, task_provider, health, name`. This story introduces `repositories[]` as a first-class, ordered list: each entry `%{id, path, default_branch, vcs: %{adapter, remote, pr: %{enabled, base_branch, draft}, task_provider: nil | map}` with exactly one `primary: true` entry. A project registered the old way (only `path`) MUST project as a single-element list `[%{id: "main", path: path, primary: true, ...}]` synthesised at READ time so nothing existing changes and no historical event is rewritten. CRITICAL replay fact verified in event_codec.ex:162-256: `decode!/2` REJECTS unknown input keys (`reject_unknown_keys!`) and raises on missing `@enforce_keys`; therefore (a) any new field added to a stored event must be a declared non-enforced struct field (old events lacking it still decode), and (b) an OLD binary replaying a NEW event with extra keys would raise - rollback of the release after repositories are written is NOT safe; document that. `default_branch` is stored but read nowhere in lib/ (scout) - this story makes the primary repo's default_branch the one consumed by E12-S3. S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: (1) if S3 picks dedicated events `ProjectRepositoryAdded/Removed` (+ aggregate commands `project.repo.add|remove`), implement those; if S3 picks 'repositories inside ProjectUpdated.config', implement a whitelist normaliser in `Aggregates.Project.handle_command("project.update")` instead and skip the new event structs. (2) S3 fixes the repo `id` charset/limit and whether `path` must be unique across projects.

---

- project.register without repositories projects exactly one repo (id main, primary true) equal to the old path

title: [E12-S10] A thread adds a repository to itself: operator allowlist and audit event
description:
Claude lets a thread add a repo to itself. Foreman must not let an agent widen its own write access silently. Design: the project holds an operator-managed allowlist `config.repo_allowlist` = list of absolute path PREFIXES or remote URL patterns (default EMPTY = feature off); a thread (agent via MCP tool `foreman_run_request_repo`, or the coordinator on its behalf) issues command `run.repo.request` (system-authored, in MCP `Policy @write_tools` because it mutates; NOT merge/approve) with `{run_id, repo_path | repo_id}`. The aggregate/side-effect step: (1) if `repo_id` already registered on the project -> attach to the run (create worktree via E12-S3 lazy path) ; (2) if `repo_path` is not registered but matches the allowlist AND is a git work tree -> `project.repo.add` (system, `added_by: run:<id>`) then attach; (3) otherwise reject `{:error, {:repo_not_allowed, path}` and still write the audit event. EVERY request, allowed or denied, appends a typed `RunRepoRequested` audit event (modelled on `JobsiteRequestAudited`/`aggregates/jobsite_audit.ex`: stream `run_repo_audit:<run_id>`, fields run_id, project_id, requested_path, repo_id, decision `allowed|denied`, reason, requested_by, at) via a new aggregate prefix registered in `command_router.ex aggregate_module_for/1` with a `_ -> state` catch-all. The operator can add to the allowlist only through `project.update` config (operator command). A run can attach at most `config.max_repos_per_run` (default 4) repos. S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: lazy secondary worktrees (needed here) vs eager-only: if S3 chooses eager-only, a mid-run attach must instead create the worktree immediately in the side-effect step and take effect for the NEXT phase's env; if S3 chooses a synthetic parent cwd the agent sees the new repo only on the next phase either way - state this in the tool description.

---

acceptance_criteria:
- empty allowlist: every request denied and audited
- allowed path outside registered repos is registered then attached, both audited
- attached repo appears in FOREMAN_REPOS next phase and gets its own PR
- tool is a write tool, never merge/approve

title: [E12-S11] Goal fan-out: one thread per repository as a special case
description:
Independent per-repo work (e.g. 'bump the lint config in every repo') does not need a single multi-repo run: it is N single-repo runs. This story provides the Foreman-side primitive the E15 coordinator (and operators) use: command `task.fanout` with `{project_id, title, prompt, workflow_name, repo_ids | "all"}` that creates ONE task per repository (each with `repo_id` from E12-S9, `external_id` nil, deterministic task ids `<fanout_id>-<repo_id>` and command ids so a retry creates no duplicates), links them with a shared `fanout_id` carried in the task input, and reports the created task ids. Distinguish from true multi-repo: fan-out runs are independent (each its own PR, no shared worktree set, merge independent, one failing does not affect others); true multi-repo is chosen when the change must land together. No new aggregate: it is a system command that loops `task.create` through `CommandGateway.dispatch_system` (so project pause/archive checks, thread caps from E1/E14 and approve gating apply per task and a cap rejection mid-way is reported per repo, with the already-created tasks kept). Exposed as CLI `foreman project fanout`? NO - exposed as operator command via /api/commands and MCP write tool `foreman_task_fanout` (write set); E15 calls the MCP tool. Needs E15 'start thread' action vocabulary to include fan-out; this story provides the tool only. S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: none to the mechanism; if S3 rejects per-repo task `repo_id` in v1, fan-out cannot target repos and this story must be dropped - confirm against E12-S9 outcome.

---

title: [E12-S12] Live multi-repo end-to-end on scratch repositories
description:
Proof that the pieces compose against real git and a real provider, not stubs. title: [E12-S3] One worktree per repository per run: creation, state, resume and cleanup
description:
A run provisions exactly ONE worktree today: `RunExecutor.create_run_worktree` (run_executor.ex ~2270-2300) calls `Worktree.create/1` (workflow/worktree.ex:69) with `operation_id: "wt-" <> run_id`, `repo_path: project_root`, `worktree_path: run_worktree_path/3`, `base_ref`, `branch`; the result is stored as `state.run_worktree` (a map: operation_id, worktree_path, branch, base_ref, project_root, project_id, implementation_key, trd_scope, cleanup). `resolve_run_base/2` derives project_root from the frozen `plan_context["project_root"]`, else the project projection path (run_executor.ex:2395-2412), and `vcs_working_directory/1` (:2141) and `project_path/1` (:2145) drive every git call (AutoPR, resolve_revision :2514, signal_pr_ready :1562). `Events.WorktreeCreated` documents 'one worktree per RUN' and `find_resumable_worktree/1` rehydrates it. This story generalises to `state.run_worktrees :: %{repo_id => worktree_map}` while keeping `state.run_worktree` as a read alias for the PRIMARY repo so single-repo behaviour is bit-for-bit unchanged. Operation ids: primary keeps `wt-<run_id>` (existing event logs and `clean_for_run/1` :227 keep working); additional repos use `wt-<run_id>-<repo_id>`. Worktree paths stay under the same managed root, `assert_worktree_path_contained` applies per repo. Provisioning policy: PRIMARY eagerly by the first phase (unchanged); secondary repos are created per the S3 decision (eagerly vs on first touch). Partial failure while creating repo N compensates (cleans) repos already created in this call and fails the phase with `{:multi_repo_worktree_failed, repo_id, reason}` - never a half-provisioned run. S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: eager vs lazy secondary worktree creation (lazy needs a `run.repo.touch` signal from E12-S10 and changes when WorktreeCreated for secondaries appears); whether a secondary repo's branch name is `<primary-branch>` (same name everywhere) or `<primary-branch>-<repo_id>`; whether `WorktreeCreated`/`WorktreeCleaned` gain `repo_id` (default here: a new optional non-enforced field `repo_id`, nil for legacy).

title: [E12-S4] Multi-repo env contract and prompt context
description:
Agents learn their workspace from env: `foreman_env/4` (run_executor.ex:2924-2990) builds `FOREMAN_WORKTREE=1, FOREMAN_RUN_ID, FOREMAN_WORKTREE_PATH, FOREMAN_EXPECTED_BRANCH, FOREMAN_SOURCE_REVISION, FOREMAN_IMPLEMENTATION_KEY, FOREMAN_ARTIFACT_PATH` (+ plan env, base-branch env, shell-session env, beads db path) and `bind_vfs(run_id, worktree_path)` binds ONE worktree. Contract for multi-repo (kept additive so every existing var still means the primary repo): `FOREMAN_WORKTREE_PATH` = primary worktree (primary stays primary), NEW `FOREMAN_REPOS` = JSON object `{repo_id: {path, branch, base_ref, base_branch, primary}` for every repo in the run, NEW `FOREMAN_PRIMARY_REPO` = primary id. Single-repo runs emit `FOREMAN_REPOS` with one entry too (harmless, lets one prompt work in both worlds) - but NO existing var changes value. The prompt gets the same information: `prompt_template_assigns/…` (run_executor.ex ~:1921, scout) gains a `repositories` list (id, path, branch, primary) that E3's `ProjectContext` builder renders ('Repositories you may modify'); this story provides the data, E3 owns the rendering/budgeting. The vfs binding must expose all worktrees or the agent cannot edit secondary repos. S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: whether the agent's cwd is the primary worktree (default) or a synthetic parent directory containing every worktree as a subdirectory; whether secondary worktrees are mounted read-only until touched. If S3 chooses a synthetic parent, `FOREMAN_WORKTREE_PATH` semantics and `bind_vfs` change accordingly.

title: [E12-S5] One branch and one PR per touched repository, with per-repo association
description:
Finalisation today assumes one PR: `finalize_run/1` (run_executor.ex ~1448-1500) calls `AutoPR.maybe_create_pr/1` (workflow/auto_pr.ex:103; gh pr create, base = run base branch, noop when no commits ahead), then `record_pr_association` (`PrAssociate.store/2`, pr_associate.ex:34, which keys the aggregate id `"pr_association:#{run_id}"` - ONE association per run, comment at line 31) and `signal_pr_ready` (:1562) dispatching `run.pr.ready` with `Identity.run_pr_ready_command_id(run_id)`. Stacked phases use `PhasePR.maybe_create/1` (phase_pr.ex:92) and `aggregates/phase_pr.ex`. This story makes finalisation iterate the run's repos: a repo is TOUCHED when it has commits ahead of its base (reuse AutoPR's ahead check) - untouched repos get no PR and no association. Each touched repo gets its own branch name (S3), PR title/body (the body lists the sibling PRs of the same run as cross-links once all exist, best-effort via `gh pr edit`), association `pr_association:<run_id>` for the primary (legacy key preserved) and `pr_association:<run_id>:<repo_id>` for others, and its own `run.pr.ready` with a per-repo deterministic command id. `ProjectionStore.pr_association/1` (projection_store.ex:352) stays run-keyed for primary; add `pr_associations_for_run/1` returning all (repo_id, pr_url, pr_number). S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: association key shape (`pr_association:<run>:<repo>` vs a list inside one association event); whether PhasePR (stack_pr: true) is supported in multi-repo runs at all (default here: stack_pr is primary-repo-only and a multi-repo run with stack_pr is rejected at workflow validation with a typed error, because stacked per-phase PRs across repos have no defined base chain).

title: [E12-S6] Merge gate per PR (operator-only) and cross-repo partial-completion semantics
description:
The merge gate is a single state on the run aggregate: `Aggregates.Run` carries `merge_gate` (nil|:pending|:approved; run.ex:37,56,97,103,238), `run.pr.ready` (:566-575) calls `PrGate.record_pending(run_id, pr_url)` into the ETS `Workflow.MergeGate` (keyed by pr_url - good), `merge_approve` (:588) requires `ensure_merge_gate_pending/1` (:758) and `ApproverAuthorizer.authorize/1`, and `run.pr.merge` is allowed only when `state.merge_gate == :approved` (`ensure_pr_gate_ok`, :742-750); the real merge is `RunPrMerge.execute/1` (pins `--match-head-commit`, refuses conflicted/closed/head-moved), invoked from `CommandGateway.perform_operator_side_effects` (:140). With N PRs one scalar cannot hold N gates. This story turns the gate into a map keyed by `repo_id` (primary key `nil`→""/primary id preserves the legacy single-gate behaviour) so each PR is approved and merged independently, each pinned to its own head sha, and the gate stays OPERATOR-ONLY: `merge_approve` and `run.pr.merge` are never MCP tools and never auto-dispatched, and nothing may add a 'merge all' shortcut that approves without per-PR identity. Cross-repo failure semantics: the run's terminal status is `completed` when every touched repo's PR was created; if PR creation failed for some repos the run records `partial` information WITHOUT a new run status (status enum is shared by projections/dashboard): `PrCreateFailed`-style data lives on the per-repo PR record (`pr_state: :open | :create_failed | :merged | :closed | :conflicted`), a run with any `create_failed` repo is `completed_with_errors` in the operator dashboard/overview derived view only, and the operator can retry a single repo with `run.pr.retry --repo-id` (operator-only, re-runs AutoPR for that repo from its preserved worktree - so worktree cleanup for a repo is DEFERRED until its PR exists or the operator discards it). S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: gate-as-map inside the run aggregate (default here) vs a new `run_pr:<run>:<repo>` aggregate per PR (then run.ex gate code is untouched and `merge_approve`/`run.pr.merge` payloads carry the new aggregate id); whether merging PRs must be ordered (dependency order declared by repos[].merge_after) or free-form (default free-form with cross-links, ordering is the operator's call); the exact partial-completion vocabulary.

---

- single-PR run: merge flow identical to today
- N PRs: each approved/merged independently, head-pinned per PR
- merge_approve/run.pr.merge remain operator-only; no MCP exposure
- repo with create_failed PR is visible, retryable, and its worktree is kept
- cleanup waits for per-repo PR resolution policy

title: [E12-S8] Review archive diff per repo and Jobsite multi-repo spec
description:
Review capture is single-checkout: `Review.Capture.close_run/2` (review/capture.ex:143) reads `state.run_worktree` and `capture_run_diff/3` (:313) writes `diff.patch` + `changed-files.txt` for one worktree/base (`put_diff/4` :85, `do_put_diff` :348 using `Jobsite.Git.diff/3`/`changed_files/3`), the manifest has one `branch/base_ref/worktree_path` (:273-274) and `Review.Analyzer` grades that archive. Multi-repo: write `diff.patch`/`changed-files.txt` for the PRIMARY repo unchanged (so the analyzer prompt and existing archives are untouched) AND `diffs/<repo_id>.patch` + `diffs/<repo_id>.files.txt` per extra repo, with a manifest `repositories: [%{id, branch, base_ref, worktree_path, diff_status, pr_url}]` (additive key; manifest is `foreman.review.manifest.v1`, schema stays v1 because the key is additive and absent for legacy). The analyzer prompt template (`priv/review/analysis_prompt.md`) gains a clause telling the evaluator to read every `diffs/*.patch`. Jobsite door: `Jobsite.Spec` whitelists keys (`@allowed_keys` spec.ex:42; `repo_path`/`path`/`base` are FORBIDDEN keys, :47) and resolves ONE repo from `project_id` (:64 resolve_project); the executor's `Worktree`/`Engine`/`Observer` assume one worktree (`Observer.step_completed(%{kind: :commit}, ...)` captures its diff). Add an optional spec key `repositories` (list of repo ids of the project; default = primary only) - ids not registered on the project are `{:error, Error.new(:spec_option_invalid, ...)}` (reuse the existing code). A jobsite with >1 repo runs one worktree per repo with the agent cwd at the primary and `FOREMAN_REPOS` passed through the runner env; commits/push/diff capture iterate repos; no PR is opened by the jobsite door (unchanged).

S3 outcome changes: the on-disk layout of per-repo diffs and manifest key names must follow S3's written decision; if S3 declares jobsite multi-repo out of scope for v1, drop the jobsite tasks (T3,T4) and keep a typed rejection `{:error, Error.new(:spec_option_invalid, 'repositories unsupported')}` for a multi-element list. title: [E12-S9] Task-provider and BeadsWatcher scoping per repository
description:
A project binds one task provider (`ProjectRegistered.task_provider`, resolved by `TaskProvider.Registry.project_config(project_id)`) and `BeadsWatcher` (task_providers/beads_watcher.ex; label `foreman-exec`) turns a bead into `task.create` with `external_id` = bead id; the review feature posts bead comments and opens gap beads through that same provider (Review.BeadSink). With repositories[] each repo MAY carry an optional `task_provider` binding (different `.beads` database per repo). Rules: (1) a repo without its own binding inherits the project's provider (so single-repo and unbound repos behave exactly as today); (2) a bead from repo X's provider creates a task whose `repo_id` hint is X and whose run's PRIMARY repo is X (other repos are added by the thread via E12-S10 or the operator) - the primary of a run is therefore not always the project's primary repo; (3) BeadSink writes comments/gap beads to the provider of the run's primary repo; (4) the BeadsWatcher loop-guard semantics for `foreman-gap` are unchanged. This needs a `primary_repo_id` on the task/run (task.create optional `repo_id`, default = project primary) which E12-S3 uses to pick the primary worktree/entry. Needs E15 coordinator awareness (coordinator may set `repo_id` when starting a thread). S3 gate: this story MUST NOT start before docs/spikes/S3.md exists with a GO/choice; the S3 outcome decides the points named under 'S3 outcome changes' and the implementer must follow the written decision, not the default stated here.

S3 outcome changes: whether per-repo provider binding exists in v1 at all (S3 may defer it: then this story reduces to the `repo_id` on task.create + resolution order and the per-repo binding tasks T3-T4 are dropped); how a bead maps to a repo when both repos' providers contain beads with the same id.

---

- repos without binding inherit project provider

Alternatives considered | Option | Approach | Verdict | |---|---|---| | **A** | In-process Phoenix `ProjectController`; mutations via existing `CommandGateway.dispatch_operator/2`; Go CLI subcommand grouping; web-layer CQRS test mirrors `event_store_enforcement_test.exs` | **Selected** — minimal new surface; matches existing `task`/`run` resource-route pattern; zero new infrastructure | | B | Action-based JSON-RPC façade (`POST /api/projects` with `action` field) | Rejected — breaks existing CLI conventions; harder to cache; deviates from `AGENTS.md` spirit | | C | Separate "projects-api" Phoenix sub-app | Rejected — violates "no new infrastructure" from `AGENTS.md`; doubles Bearer-plug/pipeline surface | ### 2b. System architecture (Option A) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph GoCLI["foreman CLI (packages/foreman_cli)"] Create["foreman project create"] Get["foreman project get"] Update["foreman project update"] Delete["foreman project delete"] List["foreman project list"] end subgraph Phoenix["foreman_server_web (Phoenix)"] Router["router.ex

+ projection store")] end Create --> CC Update --> CC Delete --> CC Get --> Router List --> Router Router --> PC PC --> PS CC --> CG CG --> CR CR --> PAct CR --> RAct PAct --> Events RAct --> Events PS --> Events DISP --> RA RA -->|step 1: project.reserve_run| CR RA -->|step 2: run.start
(deterministic command_id
from reservation)| CR RA -->|on definitive rejection only:
project.release_run_reservation| CR Events -->|terminal events
(carry project_id + run_id)| RLR RLR -->|terminal-event release:

RunAdmission.start(recovered_payload)| RA classDef new fill:#fff4e1,stroke:#d68500,stroke-width:2px class RA,RLR new ``` **Data flow:** - **Read (`GET /api/projects/:id`):** Phoenix router → `ProjectController.show/2` → `project_store.get/1` (no event appended, no command dispatched). - **Read (`GET /api/projects`):** Phoenix router → `ProjectController.index/2` → `project_store.list/0` (filtered by `include_archived?`; capped by `projects_list_max` config, default 1000). **`X-Total-Count` exposes the underlying full count of matching rows** (NOT the truncated body length); the body itself is capped at the configured limit and signals truncation via `meta.truncated: true`. - **Mutation (`POST /api/commands` with `project.update` / `project.archive`):** Phoenix router → `CommandController.create/2` → `CommandGateway.dispatch_operator/2` → identity validator (`validate_aggregate_id/1` for the new types) → `CommandRouter` → aggregate actor → event store. - **Run start (workflow dispatcher):** `Workflow.Dispatcher` → `RunAdmission.start/2` → step 1: `project.reserve_run` → step 2: `run.start` (deterministic `command_id` derived from the reservation, NO `admission:` sentinel — v1.0.1 removed it) → both dispatched via `CommandRouter.dispatch_run_start/2` → `defp do_dispatch/2` → respective aggregate actors → event store. **Compensation policy (definitive-rejection allowlist):** only `:phase_terminal` and `:run_already_terminal` failures at step 2 trigger `project.release_run_reservation` (step 3). All other failures (timeout, crash, transient) RETAIN the reservation; the reconciler scheduled pass retries `RunAdmission.start(recovered_payload)` with the deterministic `command_id` from `Project.State.active_run_reservations[run_id]` (actor-level event dedup absorbs concurrent retries). The reservation is never released on absence alone — that would race a successful `run.start` and orphan the run. - **Reconciler (two access paths, one authoritative source):** - **Subscription path (sub-second happy path):** `RunLifecycleReconciler` subscribes to `RunCompleted`, `RunFailed`, `RunCancelled`, `RunBlocked`, `RunFlaggedStuck` → reads `project_id` + `run_id` directly from the terminal event payload (no `ProjectionStore.run_projection/1` — terminal events carry `project_id`) → dispatches `project.release_run_reservation`. - **Scheduled path (60s crash recovery):** enumerates candidates via `ProjectionStore.list_projects_with_active_runs/0` → loads authoritative state via `Project.load(project_id)` (for the reservation metadata to re-dispatch) and `Run.load(run_id)` (to confirm the run is truly absent vs. just unsubscribed) → if `Run.State.exists? == false`, retries `RunAdmission.start(recovered_payload)` with the deterministic `command_id` from the reservation. Never reads `project_id` from `ProjectionStore.run_projection/1`. **Single mutation surface:** `POST /api/commands` (per `AGENTS.md`). title: [E8] Needs-you: approvals and questions
description:
Claude surfaces 'Waiting on you' when a thread needs an approval or an answer. Foreman has the ingredients but nothing connected: `Aggregates.ToolCall` (tool.request/approve/deny/finish) has no producers, no CommandRouter prefix, is in neither operator allowlist and only `ToolCallFinished` has a typed event; approvals are otherwise static per-phase `approval_mode` (interpreter.ex:477-506, run_executor.ex:1194-1209) so an unattended agent in default mode 'reports itself blocked'; the operator-question flow (OperatorQuestionSubscriber -> OperatorQuestionDispatcher -> SharedInbox) ends in `OperatorTimeout`, an ETS timer whose expiry only logs 'no-op'; there is no answer command, no pending state, and no operator->agent delivery. This epic delivers: (1) ToolCall wired end to end (router prefix `tool_call:`, typed events incl. new ToolCallExpired, operator `tool.approve|deny` in BOTH command_gateway @allowed_operator_types and command_controller @allowed_types/aggregate_prefix/composite aggregate id); (2) pending-approval projection + HTTP/MCP read tools feeding E7's 'Waiting on you'; (3) producers and decision delivery gated by spike S2 - GO: live `Session.respond_approval`; NO-GO: pause + resume-with-one-phase `approval_mode` override via E6 steering; MIXED: per provider via `Approvals.Capability`; (4) a first-class operator question aggregate with `question.answer` delivered by steer or reply signal; (5) durable sweeper-based timeouts that surface (:surface default, :deny optional) instead of silently doing nothing. Constraints: CQRS via CommandGateway, typed events with @enforce_keys, `_ -> state` catch-alls, prefixes registered in command_router.ex aggregate_module_for/1; allowlists in both places; MCP gets read tools only (NEVER approve/answer/merge via MCP, AGENTS.md); `tool.approve` is not the merge gate, which stays operator-only and untouched; secrets: tool input summaries are redacted and bounded; tests use start_supervised! and injected clocks, no sleeps. Needs E6 (steering mailbox, thread read model) and E7 (Overview classifier and Signals).

---

acceptance_criteria:
- an agent permission need or operator question appears as pending state in the API and Overview (waiting_on_you)
- operator tool.approve/deny and question.answer reach the agent per the S2 outcome and finish the call
- expired approvals/questions surface durably and survive restart
- no MCP write tool for approve/answer; merge gate untouched; both allowlists updated
- documentation gate satisfied
notes: S2 DECIDED (docs/spikes/S2.md): v1 steering = pause+resume with the operator message as the resumed prompt; pi has NO approvals (E8 live approvals only for ACP-style providers; pi path needs the NO-GO route: resume with a one-phase approval_mode override). Live Session.steer is v2, pi-only, blocked on pi-transport fixes. approval_timeout_ms must be set explicitly.

title: [E8-S1] Wire Aggregates.ToolCall: prefix, typed events, operator commands
description:
`Aggregates.ToolCall` exists (aggregates/tool_call.ex) with commands `tool.request`, `tool.approve`, `tool.deny`, `tool.finish`, stream id `tool_call:<run_id|global>:<tool_call_id>` (colons in ids escaped to `%3A`), and state machine requested -> approved|denied -> finished, but it has no producers, no CommandRouter prefix, is absent from both operator allowlists, and only `ToolCallFinished` has a typed event struct (events/tool_call_finished.ex; verified: no `tool_call_requested/approved/denied` files under events/). Wire it: (1) register `def aggregate_module_for("tool_call:" <> _)` in command_router.ex (~571-592); (2) add typed structs `ToolCallRequested` (run_id, tool_call_id, tool_name, input summary, requested_by/agent, requested_at, project_id, provider), `ToolCallApproved`, `ToolCallDenied` (decided_by, reason, decided_at) and a new `ToolCallExpired` + command `tool.expire` (system-only; allowed from status requested; terminal) following events/review_recorded.ex conventions; (3) the aggregate stays catch-all (`_ -> state`, already present) and gains the expire clause, public `ToolCall.stream_id/2` so producers/controllers build the id without reimplementing `escape/1`; (4) operator commands `tool.approve` and `tool.deny` into command_gateway.ex `@allowed_operator_types` (line 53) AND command_controller.ex `@allowed_types` (:25) + `aggregate_prefix/1` -> "tool_call" + a composite aggregate id (`id_field_for/1` returns a single field today - add a `aggregate_id_for(type, payload)` helper for the composite case and a `validate_aggregate_id` clause in the gateway like inbox.send at ~434); `tool.request`, `tool.finish`, `tool.expire` remain system-only. Approving here records the decision; delivering it to a live agent is E8-S3 (S2-gated). Important: `tool.approve` is an approval of an AGENT TOOL CALL, distinct from the operator-only merge gate (`merge_approve`/`run.pr.merge`), which is unchanged; never expose tool.approve/deny as MCP tools (AGENTS.md: never approve via MCP).

---

title: [E8-S3] Approval requests from agents and delivery of decisions (S2-gated)
description:
Producers and delivery. Today approvals are static per phase (`approval_mode` validated at interpreter.ex:477-506 and applied at run_executor.ex:1194-1209; modes default|prompt|auto_edit|auto_approve in jobsite/agent.ex) and an unattended `default` Claude 'reports itself blocked'. Spike S2 decides whether `Jido.Harness.Session.respond_approval` (plus `steer`) works headlessly for pi and claude; `AgentRuntime.JidoHarness.Session` (agent_runtime/jido_harness/session.ex:47-86) wraps only start/send_message/continue and nothing in prod uses it. What each S2 outcome changes: GO (per provider): add `Session.respond_approval/3`, run the agent turn through Session so approval requests arrive as harness events; an `Approvals.Requester` (inside the worker adapter, `overwatch/adapters/jido_harness_worker.ex` / jobsite AgentRunner, whichever S2 proves) dispatches `tool.request` and blocks the turn; an `Approvals.Deliverer` ProjectionStore subscriber on `ToolCallApproved|Denied` calls `respond_approval` and dispatches `tool.finish`. NO-GO (a provider cannot answer approvals live): there are no live prompts; `tool.request` is produced from the 'agent reported blocked on tool X' signal (run blocked with a tool-permission reason - [UNVERIFIED] where today's blocked reason is emitted; find in run_executor.ex around the phase failure path) and `tool.approve` is delivered through steer v1: the run is resumed (E6-S4 mailbox) with an `approval_mode` override for that phase (`auto_edit` or `auto_approve`, bounded to the single resumed phase, recorded on the event) plus a steering line naming the approved tool; `tool.deny` resumes with a message forbidding it. MIXED: capability per provider, GO path for the supported ones, NO-GO path for the rest, selected by `Approvals.Capability.mode(provider)`. Both paths end the same way: ToolCall aggregate holds the decision, projection shows it, the run proceeds or is told no. Expose the mode to clients (`approval_delivery: "live" | "resume_with_override"`) so the UI does not promise live prompts it cannot deliver. Needs E6 (steering mailbox) for the fallback.

Add aggregate `question:<run_id|global>:<question_id>` (register `"question:" <> _` in command_router.ex) with commands `question.open` (system, emitted by the dispatcher in addition to the inbox ingest), `question.answer` (operator: payload run_id, question_id, text <= 8000, answered_by), `question.expire` (system); typed events `QuestionOpened`, `QuestionAnswered`, `QuestionExpired`; catch-all `_ -> state`; answering twice -> `{:question_not_open, status}`. Delivery of the answer: the question carries `agent_id` and optionally a run association; if the asking agent belongs to a live workflow run, deliver via `run.steer` (E6-S4) with text 'Answer to your question <id>: ...'; for signal-bus agents publish a reply CloudEvent on the operator reply topic [UNVERIFIED: read agents/jido_signal_topics.ex for an existing reply topic; add `foreman_operator_reply` only if none]. title: [E8-S5] Timeouts that surface instead of silently no-op
description:
`OperatorTimeout` is an in-memory ETS timer GenServer (agents/operator_timeout.ex, `@default_timeout_ms` 5 min; resolved per workflow manifest `operator_timeout_ms` in the dispatcher) whose expiry only logs a warning; timers are lost on restart; tool-call requests have no timeout at all. Replace with durable, visible expiry. `Approvals.Sweeper` (GenServer, interval `:foreman_server, :approvals, sweep_interval_ms`, injectable `now_fun`) lists pending tool calls (E8-S2 reader) and open questions (E8-S4 reader) older than their timeout (`tool_call_timeout_ms` default 30 min, question timeout from `operator_timeout_ms` manifest value else 5 min as today) and dispatches `tool.expire` / `question.expire` via `dispatch_system` with `command_id: "expire:<kind>:<id>"` (idempotent, restart-safe because state is in the event log, not ETS). `OperatorTimeout.schedule/3` is kept only as the fast path: its `:expire` handler dispatches `question.expire` instead of logging a no-op, and the misleading parameter names are fixed (question_id, agent_id). Config `on_timeout: :surface | :deny` (default :surface): :surface leaves the thread in Waiting on you with reason :approval_expired / :question_expired (add these two reasons to `Overview.Group.reasons/0`; E7-S2 owns the set - Needs E7) and notifies via the existing event stream (E10 later maps these events to Messaging); :deny additionally dispatches `tool.deny` with reason "timeout" (system actor) and resumes the run with a denial message (steer v1). An expired call can no longer be approved (aggregate rejects `{:tool_call_terminal, "expired"}`) - the operator re-requests by resuming/steering. Run pause for awaiting_approval (E8-S3 NO-GO path) is not auto-resumed on expiry unless :deny.
